It's understandable to feel worried, and you're right to pay attention to these changes. Beyond memory issues, watch for difficulty with familiar tasks, confusion about time or place, mood or personality changes, trouble finding words, poor judgment, withdrawal from activities, and problems with planning or problem-solving.

When talking with your mom, try framing it around her wellbeing rather than a diagnosis. You might say, "I love you and want to make sure you're healthy. Since you've missed some appointments, let's go together for a check-up." Offering to accompany her can reduce anxiety. Some people respond better to the idea of a "baseline cognitive check" rather than "dementia screening." If she's resistant, a trusted doctor or family friend might help. Early evaluation can rule out reversible causes like medication interactions or vitamin deficiencies, and if it is dementia, early planning makes a real difference.
